Brain Anatomy includes labelled axial and regional illustrations. Every embedded label and adjacent structure still needs source-image review; the inventory is not an exhaustive closed list.
Arterial and venous territories vary and overlap. Patient-specific flow, patency, variant branching and supply cannot be inferred from a normative parent mesh or static map.

Linked vascular reading includes infarction, watershed, lacunar, PRES and venous thrombosis contexts. Corresponding disease modules and all lesion-dependent adjacent structures require separate reconciliation.

source_scope_issues.detail: Source segment conventions and all labelled source-image anatomy require explicit reconciliation. No fixed 16/18-segment denominator is assumed from the finite vessel groups.
Acquisition phase, lumen opacification, calcium scoring, calibrated stenosis/plaque measurements, CT-FFR and perfusion require method-specific evidence; a static model does not prove them.
Every depicted anomaly, lesion, non-atherosclerotic exception, stent/graft and adjacent anatomy needs exact case scope; draft conditional groups are not exhaustive.
Generic cardiac/extracardiac headings must be expanded into the actual structures reported in each acquisition. Coverage is not established by a broad parent label.

functional_evidence_requirements.evidence: Appropriate non-contrast CT, vessel assignment and validated method; contrast CTA or coloured mesh surfaces are not substitute measurements.
Calibrated orthogonal acquired lumen sections and appropriate reference; document motion/blooming and non-evaluable extent.
Method-specific source images and lesion-localised morphology, separate from stenosis and histological assertions.
Validated physiological analysis linked to the specific lesion/territory; static anatomy alone proves no physiological value.
Suitable acquired phases and calibration; static external walls cannot establish dynamic compression, chamber volumes or shunt significance.

targets: Every actual subsegmental bronchus/vessel and reported segment
Left nomenclature, branching, fissural and situs variants
Each stenosis, nodule, plug, mass and affected airway
Every expiratory/dynamic acquisition correspondence
Each intervention and altered residual anatomy
Acquired nodes/pleura/mediastinal or vascular conditions
Developmental and disease-specific contexts

source_scope_issues.detail: The eighteen common source segment entries are not an exhaustive invariant patient tree. Subsegmental divisions, venous/lymphatic localisation and precise territory boundaries require source/case expansion.
Combined or separate left apicoposterior and basal conventions must be reconciled with actual anatomy, rather than silently recoded or duplicated.
Expiration, central collapse, bronchoarterial ratios, small-airway visibility and CT tissue boundaries require appropriate acquired evidence and calibration, separate from static schematics.

All source-image labels and conditional wall disease, masses, developmental anomalies, surgery, valves, fibrosis and vascular consequences require full case-specific anatomy and diagnostic-context review.

functional_evidence_requirements.evidence: Calibrated orthogonal acquired lumen planes; obliquity and motion limits stated.
Matched acquired bronchus/artery level with perfusion context and additional CT morphology; no generic surface ratio.
Appropriate paired inspiratory/expiratory acquisition and adequacy; unacquired expiration cannot be reported negative.
Relevant dynamic/expiratory acquisition, matched levels and measurement method.
Appropriate contrast or functional source acquisitions; anatomical territory diagrams are not measured supply.

targets: Every primary, solid component, separate lesion and actual affected segment/subsegment
Each named invasive interface, laterality and acquired structure
Every individual node, station boundary and station 3A side; optional right station 11 subdivisions where used
Every actual metastatic lesion, organ system and acquisition field of view

source_scope_issues.detail: Named station and interface lists are a draft. Source/case meshes, actual node boundaries, vascular/neural extent and all imaged sites require expansion and specialist review.

IASLC 9th-edition card page 10 is the current definition source. Older linked node-map prose contains a 3B typo and describes 3P differently; original labels and side/border distinctions require reconciliation before image/model binding.
CT-visible component, nerve relationship, pleural contact, nodal size and effusion cannot establish microscopic invasion, histology, STAS or malignant involvement.
PET-CT, brain imaging, tissue sampling and prior scans are separate evidence; chest/upper-abdominal coverage cannot exclude whole-body disease.
The IASLC card explicitly requires permission before reproducing its figures for distribution. Source review is not a commercial reuse grant; no card image is packaged.

functional_evidence_requirements.evidence: Calibrated native planes, reconstruction and appropriate windows, with atelectasis excluded only when distinguishable.

functional_evidence_requirements.observation: node short axis and station count
functional_evidence_requirements.evidence: Actual source planes, separate station definitions and primary laterality; a node count is not an N2 station count.
Site-specific imaging confidence and confirmatory evidence when stage changing; contact geometry alone does not prove invasion.
Actual findings and diagnostic confirmation/context; fluid presence alone does not establish malignant effusion.
Complete lesion/site evidence in acquired studies with uncertainty and unseen sites stated; paired organs and multiple bone sites require organ-system review.
Pathological evidence separate from CT appearance; CT solid component or illustrative histology is not patient proof.
Known treatment/time point and actual matched prior studies; pretreatment c and post-treatment yc contexts kept distinct.

source_scope_issues.detail: Common Couinaud entries are not patient-measured territories. Source-specific vessel/duct branches, variants and boundaries need expansion and anatomical review.
Each claimed modality, phase, agent and sequence requires suitable acquired evidence. A permitted modality list is not proof of full modality/sequence coverage.
Every lesion and all actual acquired extrahepatic sites need explicit coverage; a selected target or parent-organ surface cannot waive the rest.
Source examples and category labels do not prove this patient eligibility, histology or response. General masses, untreated diagnosis and treatment response remain separate.
Original image/mask/registration rights, measured native sampling and cross-phase alignment need independent source review. Restricted AMPLIFAI annotations are not commercially cleared.

functional_evidence_requirements.evidence: Actual branching/territory and acquired orthogonal planes; schematic hepatic/portal planes do not measure source segment boundaries.
Complete eligible observation margin and phase, matched prior acquisition/date, calibration and uncertainty; do not count adjacent perfusion change.
Actual acquired phase/agent, adequacy and same-observation correspondence; unacquired or degraded phases remain unassessed.
Apply current agent/phase definitions separately; gadoxetate transitional/hepatobiliary hypointensity is not diagnostic washout.
Appropriate source sequences, b-values/ADC, in/opposed-phase and source alignment; no CT substitution or static model proof.
Actual agent, timing and source-phase adequacy; signal/background comparison rather than a fabricated uptake texture.
Appropriate acquired contrast/flow evidence, actual lumen soft tissue and uncertainty; vessel shape does not prove tumour or patency.
Actual patient risk/age/exclusions, source diagnostic evidence and treatment context. General masses and diagnostic/treatment-response algorithms remain separate.

source_scope_issues.detail: Draft parent entries are not a closed patient anatomy list; instantiate actual branches, variants and lesions.
Appropriate original CT/MRI phases and sequences are required; generic organ geometry supplies no enhancement or MRI signal.
Macroscopic fat strongly supports classic AML in context; rare RCC exceptions and microscopic fat remain distinct. Pattern is not histology.
Contact and label size do not establish invasion or metastatic state; covered field and actual venous upper extent need review.
Source images, annotations and derivatives need independent rights, native geometry and anatomical review. No complete renal source is approved.

functional_evidence_requirements.evidence: Actual side, complete lesion margins, calibrated orthogonal planes and repeatable prior correspondence.
Independent fat, blood, calcification, fluid and solid-region source evidence; no histological shortcut.
Original calibrated pre/post source phases, same-tissue ROI, noise/partial volume and pseudoenhancement uncertainty.
Actual T2, chemical shift, suppression, subtraction and DWI/ADC if acquired, with motion and field strength considered.
Original lumen/wall/tissue boundaries, actual venous level and covered upper extent.
Actual compartment/organ extension evidence; adjacency is not invasion.
Every actual acquired observation and source disease context; negative field cannot establish unacquired whole-body status.
Source pathology and clinical context distinguish overlapping solid tumour patterns and normal/infectious/vascular mimics.
